{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Saga Prefecture|Saga]]'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been [[:en:Cultural Property (Japan)|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]] (including three *[[List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|Special Historic Sites]]); [[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] spans the prefectural borders with [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*[[Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Site]]
{{nihongo2|吉野ヶ里遺跡}}
''Yoshinogari iseki'' || [[:en:Kanzaki, Saga|Kanzaki]], [[Yoshinogari, Saga|Yoshinogari]] || fortified [[Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ICP]] grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a [[National Government Parks|National Government Park]]{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher=[[Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Historical Park]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*[[Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|Nagoya Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]], [[:en:Genkai, Saga|Genkai]] || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 [[:en:Hectare|ha]]; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the [[Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum]] || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*[[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || [[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama]] || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by [[Silla]]-[[Tang dynasty|Tang]] forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama Town]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925155809/http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |archive-date=25 September 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.town.kiyama.saga.jp/site/k-kimama/kiijo.html |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite book |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |author=Aston, W.G. |author-link=William George Aston |year=1972 |orig-year=1896 |publisher=[[Tuttle Publishing|Tuttle]] |isbn=0-8048-0984-4 |volume=2 |pages=283f}} the designation includes an area of [[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] || [[File:基山 山頂.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44347145|N|130.51252934|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kii Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3085] |- | align="center"|[[Otsuboyama Kōgoishi]]
{{nihongo2|おつぼ山神籠石}}
''Otsuboyama kōgoishi'' || [[Takeo, Saga|Takeo]] || earthworks stretching 1,866 m, with stone pillar bases and [[sluice gates]]; there is a theory that construction was related to defeat at the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663{{cite web |url=http://www.city.takeo.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/pages/bunkazai/bunkazai-106.htm |script-title=ja:おつぼ山神籠石 |trans-title=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi |language=ja |publisher=[[Takeo, Saga|Takeo City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Otsuboyama Kogoishi first water gate from side.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.17811724|N|130.05648151|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2722] |- | align="center"|[[Yasunagata Site]]
{{nihongo2|安永田遺跡}}
''Yasunagata iseki'' || [[Tosu, Saga|Tosu]] || [[Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] {{nihongo|"high-tech factory"|ハイテク工場}}; bronze-casting site, discovered in 1974 and extending over an area of 4,400 m2, with five moulds for [[:en:Dōtaku|Dōtaku]] (bells) and five for [[:en:Hoko yari|hoko]] (spears); traces of bronze found on the valley floor suggest this may have been the site of the smelting works{{cite web |url=http://www.city.tosu.lg.jp/1393.htm |script-title=ja:安永田遺跡 |trans-title=Yasunagata Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Tosu, Saga|Tosu City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yasunagata Remains Park 20170423-1.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.39864472|N|130.51458072|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yasunagata Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2728] |- | align="center"|[[Yokotashimo Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|横田下古墳}}
''Yokotashimo kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || [[kofun]] or Kofun with red walls and three stone sarcophagi in which were found, in 1923, bronze mirrors and cylinders, [[magatama]] (comma-shaped beads), iron arrowheads, armour, and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]]{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |script-title=ja:横田下古墳 |trans-title=Yokotashimo Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121218234239/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |archive-date=18 December 2012 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki02.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 02 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 2 |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.43447582|N|130.03355397|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yokotashimo Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2718] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Kakiemon|Kakiemon Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|柿右衛門窯跡}}
''Kakiemon kama ato'' || [[:en:Arita, Saga|Arita]] || double [[:en:Anagama kiln|climbing kiln]]: A, with 12 firing chambers, a length of 42 metres, and an average incline of 11.5°; and B, with 21 chambers, a length of 83 metres, and an average gradient of 13°; [[saggar]]s and kiln tools have also been recovered{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=173325 |script-title=ja:柿右衛門窯跡 |trans-title=Kakiemon Kiln Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Kakiemon 01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.18093825|N|129.86871429|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kakiemon Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2731] |- | align="center"|[[Nabatake Site]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:菜畑遺跡|菜畑遺跡]]}}
''Nabatake iseki'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || acclaimed as Japan's first [[Paddy field|paddy]]; important for the understanding of the adoption of wet-rice technology, introduced from the continent; focus of the [[Matsurokan]] exhibition hall ||[[File:Nabatake Site rice field.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44858876|N|129.95790471|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2729] |- | align="center"|[[Mietsu Naval Dock]] Site
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:三重津海軍所|三重津海軍所]]跡}}
''Mietsu kaigunsho ato'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || inscribed on the [[:en:List of World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] as one of the [[Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/ |title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 August 2019}} || [[File:Mietsu Naval Dock view south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.207732|N|130.340137|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003786] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Anegawa Castle|Anegawa Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:姉川城|姉川城]]跡}}
''Anegawa-jō ato'' || [[:en:Kanzaki, Saga|Kanzaki]] || strategic site under [[Ryūzōji Takanobu]] but declined in importance after the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi#Pinnacle of power|unification of Kyūshū by Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]; the site extends 600 metres E-W and 800 N-S, with related mansions, temples and shrines, and a complex network of moats{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki03.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 3 |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=14 June 2012}}||[[File:Anegawa Castle Ruins south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.29314988|N|130.34839565|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Anegawa Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003663] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Katsunoo Castle|Katsunoo Castle Tsukushi Clan Sites]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:勝尾城|勝尾城]][[:ja:筑紫氏|筑紫氏]]遺跡}}
''Katsuno-jō Tsukushi-shi iseki'' || [[Tosu, Saga|Tosu]] || fortified at the end of the fifteenth century; attacked by the [[Shimazu clan]] in 1586 and later abandoned; excavations from 1995 have revealed an extensive site with moats, earthworks, mansions for retainers, temples and shrines{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=140467 |title=勝尾城筑紫氏遺跡 |trans-title=Katsuno Castle Tsukushi Clan Sites |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=16 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.40213518|N|130.46524915|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Katsuno Castle Chikushi Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003477] |- | align="center"|[[Nishikuma Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|西隈古墳}}
''Nishikuma kofun'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || C5 [[decorated kofun]] housing a large sarcophagus, with red pigmentation and incised decoration of triangles and circles{{cite web |url=http://kyuhaku.jmc.or.jp/d_frame.php/41/6/ |script-title=ja:西隈古墳 |trans-title=Nishikuma Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Kyushu National Museum]] |access-date=9 December 2013}} || [[File:Nishikuma-kofun stone wall.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32738344|N|130.29346106|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nishikuma Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2725] |- | align="center"|[[Taku Seibyō]]
{{nihongo2|多久聖廟}}
''Taku Seibyō'' || [[Taku, Saga|Taku]] || a [[:en:Edo Neo-Confucianism|Neo-Confucian]] school was established by {{nihongo|Taku Shigefumi|[[:ja:多久茂文|多久茂文]]}} in 1699; the [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ICP]] temple dates to 1708; [[Conservation Techniques for Cultural Properties|major repairs]] at the end of the [[Shōwa period]] were completed in 1990{{cite web |url=http://www.city.taku.lg.jp/site/view/contview.jsp?cateid=12&id=373&page=1 |script-title=ja:多久聖廟 |trans-title=Taku Seibyō |language=ja |publisher=[[Taku, Saga|Taku City]] |access-date=14 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3509 |script-title=ja:多久聖廟 |trans-title=Taku Seibyō |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 June 2012}} ||| [[File:Taku Seibyo 02.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.25974392|N|130.09758673|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Taku Seibyō}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|4]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2704] |- | align="center"|[[Obukumayama Kōgoishi]]
{{nihongo2|帯隈山神籠石}}
''Obukumayama kōgoishi'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || C7 fortifications discovered in 1941, that extend for 2.4 km and include a gate || [[File:Obukumayama Kōgoishi arranged stones.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.33361745|N|130.33454194|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Obukumayama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2717] |- | align="center"|[[Ōkuma Shigenobu#Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence|Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence]]
{{nihongo2|大隈重信旧宅}}
''Ōkuma Shigenobu kyū-taku'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || birthplace in 1838 of the [[Meiji period|Meiji]] statesman and future [[Prime minister of Japan|prime minister]]; dismantled for repairs in 1968 and open to the public alongside the {{nihongo|Ōkuma Memorial Museum|大隈記念館}} || [[File:Okuma Shigenobu Kyutaku.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.24812272|N|130.30848099|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|8]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2725] |- | align="center"|[[Nabeshima ware#Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site|Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|大川内鍋島窯跡}}
''Ōkawachi Nabeshima kama ato'' || [[:en:Imari, Saga|Imari]] || the ceramic craft technique of [[Nabeshima ware|Nabeshima]] ''iro'' ([[overglaze]]) is an [[:en:Intangible Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Intangible Cultural Property]]{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/303/112 |script-title=ja:色鍋島 |trans-title=Nabeshima iro-e |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/i/iroe.htm |title=iro-e |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=14 June 2012}} || [[File:Okawachiyama.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.23237631|N|129.89347898|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3383] |- | align="center"|[[Taniguchi Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|谷口古墳}}

''Saga-jō ato'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || || [[File:Marks on a stone wall at Saga Castle.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.245364|N|130.302229|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Saga Castle Site}} || || [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_ken_shiseki06.html] |- | align="center"|[[Hisagozuka Kofun]]

''Kurisōzui kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || || [[File:Kuri Souzui Kofun01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.396816|N|129.986507|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kurisōzui Kofun}} || || [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031643/index.html] |- |} ==Municipal Historic Sites== As of 1 May 2018, a further eighty-one Sites have been designated as being of municipal importance.{{cite web|url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/chiho_shitei/shichoson.html |title=都道府県別指定等文化財件数（市町村分）|trans-title=Number of Municipal Cultural Properties by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 May 2018 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {{Historic Sites of Japan}} ==See also== {{portal|Japan}} {{Commons Category|National historic sites in Saga prefecture}} {{Commons Category|Prefectural Historic Sites in Saga Prefecture}} * [[:en:Cultural Property (Japan)|Cultural Property (Japan)]] * [[:en:Hizen Province|Hizen Province]] * [[Saga Domain]] * [[Saga Prefectural Museum]] * [[:en:List of Cultural Properties of Japan - paintings (Saga)|List of Cultural Properties of Japan - paintings (Saga)]] * [[:en:List of Places of Scenic Beauty of Japan (Saga)|List of Places of Scenic Beauty of Japan (Saga)]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * {{in lang|ja}} [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031722/index.html Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture] {{draft categories| [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Historic Sites of Japan| Saga]] }} [[file:Joyama Katsunoo Castle and Fort seen from the foot.jpg|150px]] [[sn:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)| Saga]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]]

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Saga Prefecture|Saga]]'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been [[:en:Cultural Property (Japan)|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]] (including three *[[:en:List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|Special Historic Sites]]); [[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] spans the prefectural borders with [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*[[Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Site]]
{{nihongo2|吉野ヶ里遺跡}}
''Yoshinogari iseki'' || [[:en:Kanzaki, Saga|Kanzaki]], [[Yoshinogari, Saga|Yoshinogari]] || fortified [[Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ICP]] grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a [[National Government Parks|National Government Park]]{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher=[[Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Historical Park]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*[[Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|Nagoya Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]], [[:en:Genkai, Saga|Genkai]] || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 [[:en:Hectare|ha]]; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the [[Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum]] || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*[[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || [[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama]] || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by [[Silla]]-[[Tang dynasty|Tang]] forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama Town]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925155809/http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |archive-date=25 September 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.town.kiyama.saga.jp/site/k-kimama/kiijo.html |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite book |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |author=Aston, W.G. |author-link=William George Aston |year=1972 |orig-year=1896 |publisher=[[Tuttle Publishing|Tuttle]] |isbn=0-8048-0984-4 |volume=2 |pages=283f}} the designation includes an area of [[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] || [[File:基山 山頂.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44347145|N|130.51252934|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kii Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3085] |- | align="center"|[[Otsuboyama Kōgoishi]]
{{nihongo2|おつぼ山神籠石}}
''Otsuboyama kōgoishi'' || [[Takeo, Saga|Takeo]] || earthworks stretching 1,866 m, with stone pillar bases and [[sluice gates]]; there is a theory that construction was related to defeat at the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663{{cite web |url=http://www.city.takeo.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/pages/bunkazai/bunkazai-106.htm |script-title=ja:おつぼ山神籠石 |trans-title=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi |language=ja |publisher=[[Takeo, Saga|Takeo City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Otsuboyama Kogoishi first water gate from side.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.17811724|N|130.05648151|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2722] |- | align="center"|[[Yasunagata Site]]
{{nihongo2|安永田遺跡}}
''Yasunagata iseki'' || [[Tosu, Saga|Tosu]] || [[Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] {{nihongo|"high-tech factory"|ハイテク工場}}; bronze-casting site, discovered in 1974 and extending over an area of 4,400 m2, with five moulds for [[:en:Dōtaku|Dōtaku]] (bells) and five for [[:en:Hoko yari|hoko]] (spears); traces of bronze found on the valley floor suggest this may have been the site of the smelting works{{cite web |url=http://www.city.tosu.lg.jp/1393.htm |script-title=ja:安永田遺跡 |trans-title=Yasunagata Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Tosu, Saga|Tosu City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yasunagata Remains Park 20170423-1.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.39864472|N|130.51458072|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yasunagata Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2728] |- | align="center"|[[Yokotashimo Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|横田下古墳}}
''Yokotashimo kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || [[kofun]] or Kofun with red walls and three stone sarcophagi in which were found, in 1923, bronze mirrors and cylinders, [[magatama]] (comma-shaped beads), iron arrowheads, armour, and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]]{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |script-title=ja:横田下古墳 |trans-title=Yokotashimo Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121218234239/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |archive-date=18 December 2012 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki02.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 02 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 2 |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.43447582|N|130.03355397|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yokotashimo Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2718] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Kakiemon|Kakiemon Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|柿右衛門窯跡}}
''Kakiemon kama ato'' || [[:en:Arita, Saga|Arita]] || double [[:en:Anagama kiln|climbing kiln]]: A, with 12 firing chambers, a length of 42 metres, and an average incline of 11.5°; and B, with 21 chambers, a length of 83 metres, and an average gradient of 13°; [[saggar]]s and kiln tools have also been recovered{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=173325 |script-title=ja:柿右衛門窯跡 |trans-title=Kakiemon Kiln Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Kakiemon 01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.18093825|N|129.86871429|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kakiemon Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2731] |- | align="center"|[[Nabatake Site]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:菜畑遺跡|菜畑遺跡]]}}
''Nabatake iseki'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || acclaimed as Japan's first [[Paddy field|paddy]]; important for the understanding of the adoption of wet-rice technology, introduced from the continent; focus of the [[Matsurokan]] exhibition hall ||[[File:Nabatake Site rice field.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44858876|N|129.95790471|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2729] |- | align="center"|[[Mietsu Naval Dock]] Site
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:三重津海軍所|三重津海軍所]]跡}}
''Mietsu kaigunsho ato'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || inscribed on the [[:en:List of World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] as one of the [[Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/ |title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 August 2019}} || [[File:Mietsu Naval Dock view south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.207732|N|130.340137|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003786] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Anegawa Castle|Anegawa Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:姉川城|姉川城]]跡}}

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Saga Prefecture|Saga]]'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been [[:en:Cultural Property (Japan)|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]] (including three *[[:en:List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|Special Historic Sites]]); [[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] spans the prefectural borders with [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*[[Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Site]]
{{nihongo2|吉野ヶ里遺跡}}
''Yoshinogari iseki'' || [[:en:Kanzaki, Saga|Kanzaki]], [[Yoshinogari, Saga|Yoshinogari]] || fortified [[Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ICP]] grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a [[National Government Parks|National Government Park]]{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher=[[Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Historical Park]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*[[Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|Nagoya Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]], [[:en:Genkai, Saga|Genkai]] || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 [[:en:Hectare|ha]]; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the [[Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum]] || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*[[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || [[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama]] || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by [[Silla]]-[[Tang dynasty|Tang]] forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama Town]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925155809/http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |archive-date=25 September 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.town.kiyama.saga.jp/site/k-kimama/kiijo.html |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite book |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |author=Aston, W.G. |author-link=William George Aston |year=1972 |orig-year=1896 |publisher=[[Tuttle Publishing|Tuttle]] |isbn=0-8048-0984-4 |volume=2 |pages=283f}} the designation includes an area of [[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] || [[File:基山 山頂.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44347145|N|130.51252934|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kii Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3085] |- | align="center"|[[Otsuboyama Kōgoishi]]
{{nihongo2|おつぼ山神籠石}}
''Otsuboyama kōgoishi'' || [[Takeo, Saga|Takeo]] || earthworks stretching 1,866 m, with stone pillar bases and [[sluice gates]]; there is a theory that construction was related to defeat at the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663{{cite web |url=http://www.city.takeo.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/pages/bunkazai/bunkazai-106.htm |script-title=ja:おつぼ山神籠石 |trans-title=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi |language=ja |publisher=[[Takeo, Saga|Takeo City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Otsuboyama Kogoishi first water gate from side.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.17811724|N|130.05648151|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2722] |- | align="center"|[[Yasunagata Site]]
{{nihongo2|安永田遺跡}}
''Yasunagata iseki'' || [[Tosu, Saga|Tosu]] || [[Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] {{nihongo|"high-tech factory"|ハイテク工場}}; bronze-casting site, discovered in 1974 and extending over an area of 4,400 m2, with five moulds for [[:en:Dōtaku|Dōtaku]] (bells) and five for [[:en:Hoko yari|hoko]] (spears); traces of bronze found on the valley floor suggest this may have been the site of the smelting works{{cite web |url=http://www.city.tosu.lg.jp/1393.htm |script-title=ja:安永田遺跡 |trans-title=Yasunagata Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Tosu, Saga|Tosu City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yasunagata Remains Park 20170423-1.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.39864472|N|130.51458072|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yasunagata Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2728] |- | align="center"|[[Yokotashimo Kofun]]

''Kakiemon kama ato'' || [[:en:Arita, Saga|Arita]] || double [[:en:Anagama kiln|climbing kiln]]: A, with 12 firing chambers, a length of 42 metres, and an average incline of 11.5°; and B, with 21 chambers, a length of 83 metres, and an average gradient of 13°; [[saggar]]s and kiln tools have also been recovered{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=173325 |script-title=ja:柿右衛門窯跡 |trans-title=Kakiemon Kiln Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Kakiemon 01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.18093825|N|129.86871429|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kakiemon Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2731] |- | align="center"|[[Nabatake Site]]

''Hisagozuka kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || || || {{coord|33.563712|N|129.884877|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Hisagozuka Kofun}} || || [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_ken_shiseki06.html] |- | align="center"|[[Kishidake Old Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|岸岳古窯跡 （道納屋窯跡）}}
''Kishidake koyō ato (Michinaya kama ato)'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || || || {{coord|33.357847|N|129.970322|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kishidake Old Kiln Site}} || || [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_ken_shiseki06.html] |- | align="center"|[[Nita Haniwa Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|仁田埴輪窯跡}}
''Nita haniwa kama ato'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || || || {{coord|33.455720|N|130.049973|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nita Haniwa Kiln Site}} || || [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_ken_shiseki06.html] |- | align="center"|[[Kurisōzui Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:久里双水古墳|久里双水古墳]]}}
''Kurisōzui kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || || [[File:Kuri Souzui Kofun01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.396816|N|129.986507|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kurisōzui Kofun}} || || [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031643/index.html] |- |} ==Municipal Historic Sites== As of 1 May 2018, a further eighty-one Sites have been designated as being of municipal importance.{{cite web|url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/chiho_shitei/shichoson.html |title=都道府県別指定等文化財件数（市町村分）|trans-title=Number of Municipal Cultural Properties by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 May 2018 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {{Historic Sites of Japan}} ==See also== {{portal|Japan}} {{Commons Category|National historic sites in Saga prefecture}} {{Commons Category|Prefectural Historic Sites in Saga Prefecture}} * [[:en:Cultural Property (Japan)|Cultural Property (Japan)]] * [[:en:Hizen Province|Hizen Province]] * [[Saga Domain]] * [[Saga Prefectural Museum]] * [[:en:List of Cultural Properties of Japan - paintings (Saga)|List of Cultural Properties of Japan - paintings (Saga)]] * [[:en:List of Places of Scenic Beauty of Japan (Saga)|List of Places of Scenic Beauty of Japan (Saga)]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * {{in lang|ja}} [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031722/index.html Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture] {{draft categories| [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Historic Sites of Japan| Saga]] }} [[file:Joyama Katsunoo Castle and Fort seen from the foot.jpg|150px]] [[sn:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)| Saga]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]]

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Saga Prefecture|Saga]]'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been [[:en:Cultural Property (Japan)|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]] (including three *[[:en:List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|Special Historic Sites]]); [[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] spans the prefectural borders with [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*[[Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Site]]
{{nihongo2|吉野ヶ里遺跡}}
''Yoshinogari iseki'' || [[:en:Kanzaki, Saga|Kanzaki]], [[Yoshinogari, Saga|Yoshinogari]] || fortified [[Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ICP]] grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a [[National Government Parks|National Government Park]]{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher=[[Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Historical Park]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*[[Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|Nagoya Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]], [[:en:Genkai, Saga|Genkai]] || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 [[:en:Hectare|ha]]; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the [[Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum]] || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*[[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || [[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama]] || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by [[Silla]]-[[Tang dynasty|Tang]] forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama Town]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925155809/http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |archive-date=25 September 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.town.kiyama.saga.jp/site/k-kimama/kiijo.html |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite book |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |author=Aston, W.G. |author-link=William George Aston |year=1972 |orig-year=1896 |publisher=[[Tuttle Publishing|Tuttle]] |isbn=0-8048-0984-4 |volume=2 |pages=283f}} the designation includes an area of [[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] || [[File:基山 山頂.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44347145|N|130.51252934|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kii Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3085] |- | align="center"|[[Otsuboyama Kōgoishi]]
{{nihongo2|おつぼ山神籠石}}
''Otsuboyama kōgoishi'' || [[Takeo, Saga|Takeo]] || earthworks stretching 1,866 m, with stone pillar bases and [[sluice gates]]; there is a theory that construction was related to defeat at the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663{{cite web |url=http://www.city.takeo.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/pages/bunkazai/bunkazai-106.htm |script-title=ja:おつぼ山神籠石 |trans-title=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi |language=ja |publisher=[[Takeo, Saga|Takeo City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Otsuboyama Kogoishi first water gate from side.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.17811724|N|130.05648151|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2722] |- | align="center"|[[Yasunagata Site]]
{{nihongo2|安永田遺跡}}
''Yasunagata iseki'' || [[Tosu, Saga|Tosu]] || [[Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] {{nihongo|"high-tech factory"|ハイテク工場}}; bronze-casting site, discovered in 1974 and extending over an area of 4,400 m2, with five moulds for [[:en:Dōtaku|Dōtaku]] (bells) and five for [[:en:Hoko yari|hoko]] (spears); traces of bronze found on the valley floor suggest this may have been the site of the smelting works{{cite web |url=http://www.city.tosu.lg.jp/1393.htm |script-title=ja:安永田遺跡 |trans-title=Yasunagata Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Tosu, Saga|Tosu City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yasunagata Remains Park 20170423-1.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.39864472|N|130.51458072|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yasunagata Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2728] |- | align="center"|[[Yokotashimo Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|横田下古墳}}
''Yokotashimo kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || [[kofun]] or Kofun with red walls and three stone sarcophagi in which were found, in 1923, bronze mirrors and cylinders, [[magatama]] (comma-shaped beads), iron arrowheads, armour, and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]]{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |script-title=ja:横田下古墳 |trans-title=Yokotashimo Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121218234239/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |archive-date=18 December 2012 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki02.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 02 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 2 |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.43447582|N|130.03355397|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yokotashimo Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2718] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Kakiemon|Kakiemon Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|柿右衛門窯跡}}
''Kakiemon kama ato'' || [[:en:Arita, Saga|Arita]] || double [[:en:Anagama kiln|climbing kiln]]: A, with 12 firing chambers, a length of 42 metres, and an average incline of 11.5°; and B, with 21 chambers, a length of 83 metres, and an average gradient of 13°; [[saggar]]s and kiln tools have also been recovered{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=173325 |script-title=ja:柿右衛門窯跡 |trans-title=Kakiemon Kiln Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Kakiemon 01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.18093825|N|129.86871429|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kakiemon Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2731] |- | align="center"|[[Nabatake Site]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:菜畑遺跡|菜畑遺跡]]}}
''Nabatake iseki'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || acclaimed as Japan's first [[Paddy field|paddy]]; important for the understanding of the adoption of wet-rice technology, introduced from the continent; focus of the [[:en:Matsurokan|Matsurokan]] exhibition hall ||[[File:Nabatake Site rice field.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44858876|N|129.95790471|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2729] |- | align="center"|[[Mietsu Naval Dock]] Site
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:三重津海軍所|三重津海軍所]]跡}}
''Mietsu kaigunsho ato'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || inscribed on the [[:en:List of World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] as one of the [[Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/ |title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 August 2019}} || [[File:Mietsu Naval Dock view south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.207732|N|130.340137|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003786] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Anegawa Castle|Anegawa Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:姉川城|姉川城]]跡}}
''Anegawa-jō ato'' || [[:en:Kanzaki, Saga|Kanzaki]] || strategic site under [[Ryūzōji Takanobu]] but declined in importance after the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi#Pinnacle of power|unification of Kyūshū by Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]; the site extends 600 metres E-W and 800 N-S, with related mansions, temples and shrines, and a complex network of moats{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki03.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 3 |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=14 June 2012}}||[[File:Anegawa Castle Ruins south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.29314988|N|130.34839565|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Anegawa Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003663] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Katsunoo Castle|Katsunoo Castle Tsukushi Clan Sites]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:勝尾城|勝尾城]][[:ja:筑紫氏|筑紫氏]]遺跡}}
''Katsuno-jō Tsukushi-shi iseki'' || [[Tosu, Saga|Tosu]] || fortified at the end of the fifteenth century; attacked by the [[Shimazu clan]] in 1586 and later abandoned; excavations from 1995 have revealed an extensive site with moats, earthworks, mansions for retainers, temples and shrines{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=140467 |title=勝尾城筑紫氏遺跡 |trans-title=Katsuno Castle Tsukushi Clan Sites |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=16 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.40213518|N|130.46524915|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Katsuno Castle Chikushi Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003477] |- | align="center"|[[Nishikuma Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|西隈古墳}}
''Nishikuma kofun'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || C5 [[decorated kofun]] housing a large sarcophagus, with red pigmentation and incised decoration of triangles and circles{{cite web |url=http://kyuhaku.jmc.or.jp/d_frame.php/41/6/ |script-title=ja:西隈古墳 |trans-title=Nishikuma Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Kyushu National Museum]] |access-date=9 December 2013}} || [[File:Nishikuma-kofun stone wall.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32738344|N|130.29346106|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nishikuma Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2725] |- | align="center"|[[Taku Seibyō]]
{{nihongo2|多久聖廟}}
''Taku Seibyō'' || [[Taku, Saga|Taku]] || a [[:en:Edo Neo-Confucianism|Neo-Confucian]] school was established by {{nihongo|Taku Shigefumi|[[:ja:多久茂文|多久茂文]]}} in 1699; the [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ICP]] temple dates to 1708; [[Conservation Techniques for Cultural Properties|major repairs]] at the end of the [[Shōwa period]] were completed in 1990{{cite web |url=http://www.city.taku.lg.jp/site/view/contview.jsp?cateid=12&id=373&page=1 |script-title=ja:多久聖廟 |trans-title=Taku Seibyō |language=ja |publisher=[[Taku, Saga|Taku City]] |access-date=14 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3509 |script-title=ja:多久聖廟 |trans-title=Taku Seibyō |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 June 2012}} ||| [[File:Taku Seibyo 02.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.25974392|N|130.09758673|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Taku Seibyō}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|4]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2704] |- | align="center"|[[Obukumayama Kōgoishi]]
{{nihongo2|帯隈山神籠石}}
''Obukumayama kōgoishi'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || C7 fortifications discovered in 1941, that extend for 2.4 km and include a gate || [[File:Obukumayama Kōgoishi arranged stones.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.33361745|N|130.33454194|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Obukumayama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2717] |- | align="center"|[[Ōkuma Shigenobu#Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence|Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence]]
{{nihongo2|大隈重信旧宅}}
''Ōkuma Shigenobu kyū-taku'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || birthplace in 1838 of the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji]] statesman and future [[Prime minister of Japan|prime minister]]; dismantled for repairs in 1968 and open to the public alongside the {{nihongo|Ōkuma Memorial Museum|大隈記念館}} || [[File:Okuma Shigenobu Kyutaku.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.24812272|N|130.30848099|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|8]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2725] |- | align="center"|[[Nabeshima ware#Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site|Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|大川内鍋島窯跡}}
''Ōkawachi Nabeshima kama ato'' || [[:en:Imari, Saga|Imari]] || the ceramic craft technique of [[Nabeshima ware|Nabeshima]] ''iro'' ([[overglaze]]) is an [[:en:Intangible Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Intangible Cultural Property]]{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/303/112 |script-title=ja:色鍋島 |trans-title=Nabeshima iro-e |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/i/iroe.htm |title=iro-e |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=14 June 2012}} || [[File:Okawachiyama.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.23237631|N|129.89347898|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3383] |- | align="center"|[[Taniguchi Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|谷口古墳}}

''Saga-jō ato'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || || [[File:Marks on a stone wall at Saga Castle.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.245364|N|130.302229|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Saga Castle Site}} || || [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_ken_shiseki06.html] |- | align="center"|[[Hisagozuka Kofun]]

''Kurisōzui kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || || [[File:Kuri Souzui Kofun01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.396816|N|129.986507|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kurisōzui Kofun}} || || [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031643/index.html] |- |} ==Municipal Historic Sites== As of 1 May 2018, a further eighty-one Sites have been designated as being of municipal importance.{{cite web|url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/chiho_shitei/shichoson.html |title=都道府県別指定等文化財件数（市町村分）|trans-title=Number of Municipal Cultural Properties by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 May 2018 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {{Historic Sites of Japan}} ==See also== {{portal|Japan}} {{Commons Category|National historic sites in Saga prefecture}} {{Commons Category|Prefectural Historic Sites in Saga Prefecture}} * [[:en:Cultural Property (Japan)|Cultural Property (Japan)]] * [[:en:Hizen Province|Hizen Province]] * [[Saga Domain]] * [[Saga Prefectural Museum]] * [[:en:List of Cultural Properties of Japan - paintings (Saga)|List of Cultural Properties of Japan - paintings (Saga)]] * [[:en:List of Places of Scenic Beauty of Japan (Saga)|List of Places of Scenic Beauty of Japan (Saga)]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * {{in lang|ja}} [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031722/index.html Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture] {{draft categories| [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Historic Sites of Japan| Saga]] }} [[file:Joyama Katsunoo Castle and Fort seen from the foot.jpg|150px]] [[sn:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)| Saga]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]]

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[Saga Prefecture|Saga]]'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been [[:en:Cultural Property (Japan)|designated]] as being of national [[Values (heritage)|significance]] (including three *[[:en:List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|Special Historic Sites]]); [[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] spans the prefectural borders with [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*[[Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Site]]
{{nihongo2|吉野ヶ里遺跡}}
''Yoshinogari iseki'' || [[:en:Kanzaki, Saga|Kanzaki]], [[Yoshinogari, Saga|Yoshinogari]] || fortified [[Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ICP]] grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a [[National Government Parks|National Government Park]]{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher=[[Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Historical Park]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*[[Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|Nagoya Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]], [[:en:Genkai, Saga|Genkai]] || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 [[:en:Hectare|ha]]; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the [[Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum]] || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*[[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || [[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama]] || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by [[Silla]]-[[Tang dynasty|Tang]] forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama Town]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925155809/http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |archive-date=25 September 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.town.kiyama.saga.jp/site/k-kimama/kiijo.html |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite book |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |author=Aston, W.G. |author-link=William George Aston |year=1972 |orig-year=1896 |publisher=[[Tuttle Publishing|Tuttle]] |isbn=0-8048-0984-4 |volume=2 |pages=283f}} the designation includes an area of [[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] || [[File:基山 山頂.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44347145|N|130.51252934|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kii Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3085] |- | align="center"|[[Otsuboyama Kōgoishi]]
{{nihongo2|おつぼ山神籠石}}
''Otsuboyama kōgoishi'' || [[Takeo, Saga|Takeo]] || earthworks stretching 1,866 m, with stone pillar bases and [[sluice gates]]; there is a theory that construction was related to defeat at the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663{{cite web |url=http://www.city.takeo.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/pages/bunkazai/bunkazai-106.htm |script-title=ja:おつぼ山神籠石 |trans-title=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi |language=ja |publisher=[[Takeo, Saga|Takeo City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Otsuboyama Kogoishi first water gate from side.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.17811724|N|130.05648151|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2722] |- | align="center"|[[Yasunagata Site]]
{{nihongo2|安永田遺跡}}
''Yasunagata iseki'' || [[Tosu, Saga|Tosu]] || [[Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] {{nihongo|"high-tech factory"|ハイテク工場}}; bronze-casting site, discovered in 1974 and extending over an area of 4,400 m2, with five moulds for [[:en:Dōtaku|Dōtaku]] (bells) and five for [[:en:Hoko yari|hoko]] (spears); traces of bronze found on the valley floor suggest this may have been the site of the smelting works{{cite web |url=http://www.city.tosu.lg.jp/1393.htm |script-title=ja:安永田遺跡 |trans-title=Yasunagata Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Tosu, Saga|Tosu City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yasunagata Remains Park 20170423-1.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.39864472|N|130.51458072|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yasunagata Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2728] |- | align="center"|[[Yokotashimo Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|横田下古墳}}
''Yokotashimo kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || [[kofun]] or Kofun with red walls and three stone sarcophagi in which were found, in 1923, bronze mirrors and cylinders, [[magatama]] (comma-shaped beads), iron arrowheads, armour, and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]]{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |script-title=ja:横田下古墳 |trans-title=Yokotashimo Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121218234239/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |archive-date=18 December 2012 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki02.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 02 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 2 |language=ja |publisher=[[Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.43447582|N|130.03355397|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yokotashimo Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2718] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Kakiemon|Kakiemon Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|柿右衛門窯跡}}
''Kakiemon kama ato'' || [[:en:Arita, Saga|Arita]] || double [[:en:Anagama kiln|climbing kiln]]: A, with 12 firing chambers, a length of 42 metres, and an average incline of 11.5°; and B, with 21 chambers, a length of 83 metres, and an average gradient of 13°; [[saggar]]s and kiln tools have also been recovered{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=173325 |script-title=ja:柿右衛門窯跡 |trans-title=Kakiemon Kiln Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Kakiemon 01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.18093825|N|129.86871429|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kakiemon Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2731] |- | align="center"|[[Nabatake Site]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:菜畑遺跡|菜畑遺跡]]}}
''Nabatake iseki'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || acclaimed as Japan's first [[Paddy field|paddy]]; important for the understanding of the adoption of wet-rice technology, introduced from the continent; focus of the [[:en:Matsurokan|Matsurokan]] exhibition hall ||[[File:Nabatake Site rice field.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44858876|N|129.95790471|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2729] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Mietsu Naval Dock|Mietsu Naval Dock]] Site
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:三重津海軍所|三重津海軍所]]跡}}
''Mietsu kaigunsho ato'' || [[Saga, Saga|Saga]] || inscribed on the [[:en:List of World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] as one of the [[Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/ |title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 August 2019}} || [[File:Mietsu Naval Dock view south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.207732|N|130.340137|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003786] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Anegawa Castle|Anegawa Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:姉川城|姉川城]]跡}}
