[[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] {{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[:en:Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga]]'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been [[:en:Cultural Property (Japan)|designated]] as being of national [[:en:Values (heritage)|significance]] (including three *[[:en:List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|Special Historic Sites]]); [[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] spans the prefectural borders with [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]] |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*[[:en:Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Site]]
{{nihongo2|吉野ヶ里遺跡}}
''Yoshinogari iseki'' || [[:en:Kanzaki, Saga|Kanzaki]], [[:en:Yoshinogari, Saga|Yoshinogari]] || fortified [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ICP]] grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a [[:en:National Government Parks|National Government Park]]{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher=[[:en:Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Historical Park]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*[[:en:Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|Nagoya Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]], [[:en:Genkai, Saga|Genkai]] || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 [[:en:Hectare|ha]]; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the [[:en:Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum]] || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*[[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || [[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama]] || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by [[:en:Silla|Silla]]-[[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang]] forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama Town]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925155809/http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |archive-date=25 September 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.town.kiyama.saga.jp/site/k-kimama/kiijo.html |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite book |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |author=Aston, W.G. |author-link=William George Aston |year=1972 |orig-year=1896 |publisher=[[Tuttle Publishing|Tuttle]] |isbn=0-8048-0984-4 |volume=2 |pages=283f}} the designation includes an area of [[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] || [[File:基山 山頂.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44347145|N|130.51252934|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kii Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3085] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Otsuboyama Kōgoishi|Otsuboyama Kōgoishi]]
{{nihongo2|おつぼ山神籠石}}
''Otsuboyama kōgoishi'' || [[:en:Takeo, Saga|Takeo]] || earthworks stretching 1,866 m, with stone pillar bases and [[:en:sluice gates|sluice gates]]; there is a theory that construction was related to defeat at the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663{{cite web |url=http://www.city.takeo.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/pages/bunkazai/bunkazai-106.htm |script-title=ja:おつぼ山神籠石 |trans-title=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Takeo, Saga|Takeo City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Otsuboyama Kogoishi first water gate from side.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.17811724|N|130.05648151|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2722] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Yasunagata Site|Yasunagata Site]]
{{nihongo2|安永田遺跡}}
''Yasunagata iseki'' || [[:en:Tosu, Saga|Tosu]] || [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] {{nihongo|"high-tech factory"|ハイテク工場}}; bronze-casting site, discovered in 1974 and extending over an area of 4,400 m2, with five moulds for [[:en:Dōtaku|Dōtaku]] (bells) and five for [[:en:Hoko yari|hoko]] (spears); traces of bronze found on the valley floor suggest this may have been the site of the smelting works{{cite web |url=http://www.city.tosu.lg.jp/1393.htm |script-title=ja:安永田遺跡 |trans-title=Yasunagata Site |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Tosu, Saga|Tosu City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yasunagata Remains Park 20170423-1.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.39864472|N|130.51458072|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yasunagata Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2728] |- | align="center"|[[Yokotashimo Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|横田下古墳}}
''Yokotashimo kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || [[kofun]] or Kofun with red walls and three stone sarcophagi in which were found, in 1923, bronze mirrors and cylinders, [[magatama]] (comma-shaped beads), iron arrowheads, armour, and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]]{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |script-title=ja:横田下古墳 |trans-title=Yokotashimo Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121218234239/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |archive-date=18 December 2012 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki02.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 02 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 2 |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.43447582|N|130.03355397|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yokotashimo Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2718] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Kakiemon|Kakiemon Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|柿右衛門窯跡}}

[[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] {{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the [[:en:Prefectures of Japan|Prefecture]] of '''[[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga]]'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been [[:en:Cultural Property (Japan)|designated]] as being of national [[:en:Values (heritage)|significance]] (including three *[[:en:List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|Special Historic Sites]]); [[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] spans the prefectural borders with [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka]].{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]] |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*[[:en:Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Site]]

''Yoshinogari iseki'' || [[:en:Kanzaki, Saga|Kanzaki]], [[:en:Yoshinogari, Saga|Yoshinogari]] || fortified [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ICP]] grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a [[:en:National Government Parks|National Government Park]]{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher=[[:en:Yoshinogari site|Yoshinogari Historical Park]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*[[:en:Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|Nagoya Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]], [[:en:Genkai, Saga|Genkai]] || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 [[:en:Hectare|ha]]; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the [[:en:Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum]] || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*[[:en:Kii Castle|Kii Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || [[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama]] || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by [[:en:Silla|Silla]]-[[:en:Tang dynasty|Tang]] forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Kiyama, Saga|Kiyama Town]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925155809/http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |archive-date=25 September 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.town.kiyama.saga.jp/site/k-kimama/kiijo.html |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite book |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |author=Aston, W.G. |author-link=William George Aston |year=1972 |orig-year=1896 |publisher=[[Tuttle Publishing|Tuttle]] |isbn=0-8048-0984-4 |volume=2 |pages=283f}} the designation includes an area of [[:en:Chikushino, Fukuoka|Chikushino]] in [[:en:Fukuoka Prefecture|Fukuoka Prefecture]] || [[File:基山 山頂.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44347145|N|130.51252934|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kii Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3085] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Otsuboyama Kōgoishi|Otsuboyama Kōgoishi]]
{{nihongo2|おつぼ山神籠石}}
''Otsuboyama kōgoishi'' || [[:en:Takeo, Saga|Takeo]] || earthworks stretching 1,866 m, with stone pillar bases and [[:en:sluice gates|sluice gates]]; there is a theory that construction was related to defeat at the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663{{cite web |url=http://www.city.takeo.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/pages/bunkazai/bunkazai-106.htm |script-title=ja:おつぼ山神籠石 |trans-title=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Takeo, Saga|Takeo City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Otsuboyama Kogoishi first water gate from side.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.17811724|N|130.05648151|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2722] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Yasunagata Site|Yasunagata Site]]
{{nihongo2|安永田遺跡}}
''Yasunagata iseki'' || [[:en:Tosu, Saga|Tosu]] || [[:en:Yayoi period|Yayoi-period]] {{nihongo|"high-tech factory"|ハイテク工場}}; bronze-casting site, discovered in 1974 and extending over an area of 4,400 m2, with five moulds for [[:en:Dōtaku|Dōtaku]] (bells) and five for [[:en:Hoko yari|hoko]] (spears); traces of bronze found on the valley floor suggest this may have been the site of the smelting works{{cite web |url=http://www.city.tosu.lg.jp/1393.htm |script-title=ja:安永田遺跡 |trans-title=Yasunagata Site |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Tosu, Saga|Tosu City]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yasunagata Remains Park 20170423-1.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.39864472|N|130.51458072|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yasunagata Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2728] |- | align="center"|[[Yokotashimo Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|横田下古墳}}
''Yokotashimo kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || [[kofun]] or Kofun with red walls and three stone sarcophagi in which were found, in 1923, bronze mirrors and cylinders, [[magatama]] (comma-shaped beads), iron arrowheads, armour, and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]]{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |script-title=ja:横田下古墳 |trans-title=Yokotashimo Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121218234239/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |archive-date=18 December 2012 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki02.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 02 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 2 |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.43447582|N|130.03355397|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yokotashimo Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2718] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Kakiemon|Kakiemon Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|柿右衛門窯跡}}
''Kakiemon kama ato'' || [[:en:Arita, Saga|Arita]] || double [[:en:Anagama kiln|climbing kiln]]: A, with 12 firing chambers, a length of 42 metres, and an average incline of 11.5°; and B, with 21 chambers, a length of 83 metres, and an average gradient of 13°; [[:en:saggar|saggar]]s and kiln tools have also been recovered{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=173325 |script-title=ja:柿右衛門窯跡 |trans-title=Kakiemon Kiln Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Kakiemon 01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.18093825|N|129.86871429|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kakiemon Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2731] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Nabatake Site|Nabatake Site]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:菜畑遺跡|菜畑遺跡]]}}
''Nabatake iseki'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || acclaimed as Japan's first [[:en:Paddy field|paddy]]; important for the understanding of the adoption of wet-rice technology, introduced from the continent; focus of the [[:en:Matsurokan|Matsurokan]] exhibition hall ||[[File:Nabatake Site rice field.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44858876|N|129.95790471|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2729] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Mietsu Naval Dock|Mietsu Naval Dock]] Site
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:三重津海軍所|三重津海軍所]]跡}}
''Mietsu kaigunsho ato'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || inscribed on the [[:en:List of World Heritage Sites in Japan|UNESCO World Heritage List]] as one of the [[:en:Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining|Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/ |title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 August 2019}} || [[File:Mietsu Naval Dock view south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.207732|N|130.340137|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003786] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Anegawa Castle|Anegawa Castle]] ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:姉川城|姉川城]]跡}}
''Anegawa-jō ato'' || [[:en:Kanzaki, Saga|Kanzaki]] || strategic site under [[:en:Ryūzōji Takanobu|Ryūzōji Takanobu]] but declined in importance after the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi#Pinnacle of power|unification of Kyūshū by Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]; the site extends 600 metres E-W and 800 N-S, with related mansions, temples and shrines, and a complex network of moats{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki03.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 3 |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Saga Prefecture|Saga Prefecture]] |access-date=14 June 2012}}||[[File:Anegawa Castle Ruins south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.29314988|N|130.34839565|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Anegawa Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003663] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Katsunoo Castle|Katsunoo Castle Tsukushi Clan Sites]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:勝尾城|勝尾城]][[:ja:筑紫氏|筑紫氏]]遺跡}}
''Katsuno-jō Tsukushi-shi iseki'' || [[:en:Tosu, Saga|Tosu]] || fortified at the end of the fifteenth century; attacked by the [[:en:Shimazu clan|Shimazu clan]] in 1586 and later abandoned; excavations from 1995 have revealed an extensive site with moats, earthworks, mansions for retainers, temples and shrines{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=140467 |title=勝尾城筑紫氏遺跡 |trans-title=Katsuno Castle Tsukushi Clan Sites |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=16 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.40213518|N|130.46524915|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Katsuno Castle Chikushi Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003477] |- | align="center"|[[Nishikuma Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|西隈古墳}}
''Nishikuma kofun'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || C5 [[decorated kofun]] housing a large sarcophagus, with red pigmentation and incised decoration of triangles and circles{{cite web |url=http://kyuhaku.jmc.or.jp/d_frame.php/41/6/ |script-title=ja:西隈古墳 |trans-title=Nishikuma Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Kyushu National Museum]] |access-date=9 December 2013}} || [[File:Nishikuma-kofun stone wall.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32738344|N|130.29346106|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nishikuma Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2725] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Taku Seibyō|Taku Seibyō]]
{{nihongo2|多久聖廟}}
''Taku Seibyō'' || [[:en:Taku, Saga|Taku]] || a [[:en:Edo Neo-Confucianism|Neo-Confucian]] school was established by {{nihongo|Taku Shigefumi|[[:ja:多久茂文|多久茂文]]}} in 1699; the [[:en:Important Cultural Property (Japan)|ICP]] temple dates to 1708; [[Conservation Techniques for Cultural Properties|major repairs]] at the end of the [[:en:Shōwa era|Shōwa era]] were completed in 1990{{cite web |url=http://www.city.taku.lg.jp/site/view/contview.jsp?cateid=12&id=373&page=1 |script-title=ja:多久聖廟 |trans-title=Taku Seibyō |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Taku, Saga|Taku City]] |access-date=14 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3509 |script-title=ja:多久聖廟 |trans-title=Taku Seibyō |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 June 2012}} ||| [[File:Taku Seibyo 02.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.25974392|N|130.09758673|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Taku Seibyō}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|4]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2704] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Obukumayama Kōgoishi|Obukumayama Kōgoishi]]
{{nihongo2|帯隈山神籠石}}
''Obukumayama kōgoishi'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || C7 fortifications discovered in 1941, that extend for 2.4 km and include a gate || [[File:Obukumayama Kōgoishi arranged stones.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.33361745|N|130.33454194|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Obukumayama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2717] |- | align="center"|[[Ōkuma Shigenobu#Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence|Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence]]

''Ōkuma Shigenobu kyū-taku'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || birthplace in 1838 of the [[:en:Meiji era|Meiji]] statesman and future [[:en:prime minister of Japan|prime minister]]; dismantled for repairs in 1968 and open to the public alongside the {{nihongo|Ōkuma Memorial Museum|大隈記念館}} || [[File:Okuma Shigenobu Kyutaku.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.24812272|N|130.30848099|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|8]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2725] |- | align="center"|[[Nabeshima ware#Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site|Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|大川内鍋島窯跡}}
''Ōkawachi Nabeshima kama ato'' || [[:en:Imari, Saga|Imari]] || the ceramic craft technique of [[:en:Nabeshima ware#Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site|Nabeshima]] ''iro'' ([[:en:overglaze|overglaze]]) is an [[:en:Intangible Cultural Properties of Japan|Important Intangible Cultural Property]]{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/303/112 |script-title=ja:色鍋島 |trans-title=Nabeshima iro-e |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.aisf.or.jp/~jaanus/deta/i/iroe.htm |title=iro-e |publisher=[[Japanese Architecture and Art Net Users System]] |access-date=14 June 2012}} || [[File:Okawachiyama.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.23237631|N|129.89347898|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3383] |- | align="center"|[[Taniguchi Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|谷口古墳}}
''Taniguchi kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || seventy-seven metre, keyhole-shaped [[kofun]] with two stone chambers, boat-shaped sarcophagi, and grave goods that include mirrors, stone combs, items made of iron, and [[:en:Haji pottery|Haji pottery]], dated to the end of the fourth century || || {{coord|33.45271378|N|130.05455231|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Taniguchi Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2716] |- | align="center"|[[Chōshizuka Kofun (Saga)|Chōshizuka Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:銚子塚古墳 (佐賀市)|銚子塚古墳]]}}
''Chōshizuka kofun'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || large early [[kofun]], 98 metres long and dating to the second half of the fourth century || [[File:Choshizuka-kofun (Saga) zenkei.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.317788|N|130.29953399|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Chōshizuka Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2726] |- | align="center"|[[Tashiroōta Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:田代太田古墳|田代太田古墳]]}}
''Tashiroōta kofun'' || [[:en:Tosu, Saga|Tosu]] || triple-chambered, 42 metre [[decorated kofun]] with red ochre, carbon black and green earth paintings of triangles, concentric circles, boats, humans with outstretched arms, and figures on horseback, concentrated on the rear wall of the burial chamber{{cite web |url=http://www.city.tosu.lg.jp/1382.htm |script-title=ja:田代太田古墳 |trans-title=Tashiroōta Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[:en:Tosu, Saga|Tosu City]] |access-date=16 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://kyuhaku.jmc.or.jp/d_frame.php/41/1/ |script-title=ja:田代太田古墳 |trans-title=Tashiroōta Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Kyushu National Museum]] |access-date=9 December 2013}} || [[File:Tashiro-Ota Ancient Grave 20170423.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.39496411|N|130.51533112|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Tashiroōta Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2712] |- | align="center"|[[:en:Habu Site|Habu Site]]
{{nihongo2|土生遺跡}}

''Kurisōzui kofun'' || [[:en:Karatsu, Saga|Karatsu]] || || [[File:Kuri Souzui Kofun01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.396816|N|129.986507|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kurisōzui Kofun}} || || [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031643/index.html] |- |} ==Municipal Historic Sites== As of 1 May 2018, a further eighty-one Sites have been designated as being of municipal importance.{{cite web|url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/chiho_shitei/shichoson.html |title=都道府県別指定等文化財件数（市町村分）|trans-title=Number of Municipal Cultural Properties by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 May 2018 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {{Historic Sites of Japan}} ==See also== {{portal|Japan}} {{Commons Category|National historic sites in Saga prefecture}} {{Commons Category|Prefectural Historic Sites in Saga Prefecture}} * [[:en:Cultural Property (Japan)|Cultural Property (Japan)]] * [[:en:Hizen Province|Hizen Province]] * [[:en:Saga Domain|Saga Domain]] * [[:en:Saga Prefectural Museum|Saga Prefectural Museum]] * [[:en:List of Cultural Properties of Japan - paintings (Saga)|List of Cultural Properties of Japan - paintings (Saga)]] * [[:en:List of Places of Scenic Beauty of Japan (Saga)|List of Places of Scenic Beauty of Japan (Saga)]] ==References== {{Reflist|2}} ==External links== * {{in lang|ja}} [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031722/index.html Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture] [[file:Joyama Katsunoo Castle and Fort seen from the foot.jpg|150px]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)| Saga]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] {{wikidata link|Q6573281}} [[Category:Historic Sites of Japan| Saga]] [[Category:Pages without translation templates]] [[Category:Saga Prefecture]] [[Category:Wikidata has English label]] [[Category:Wikidata has short description]]

revision.text:
[[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] {{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the {{ill|Prefectures of Japan|en|Prefectures of Japan|WD=Q50337|lt=Prefecture}} of '''{{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga}}'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q858308|lt=designated}} as being of national {{ill|Values (heritage)|en|Values (heritage)|WD=Q7912786|lt=significance}} (including three *{{ill|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|en|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|WD=Q20982902|lt=Special Historic Sites}}); {{ill|Kii Castle|en|Kii Castle|WD=Q11426463|lt=Kii Castle}} spans the prefectural borders with {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka}}.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}} |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Yoshinogari site|en|Yoshinogari site|WD=Q1049645|lt=Yoshinogari Site}}
{{nihongo2|吉野ヶ里遺跡}}
''Yoshinogari iseki'' || {{ill|Kanzaki, Saga|en|Kanzaki, Saga|WD=Q990392|lt=Kanzaki}}, {{ill|Yoshinogari, Saga|en|Yoshinogari, Saga|WD=Q1206915|lt=Yoshinogari}} || fortified {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|WD=Q207858|lt=Yayoi-period}} settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=ICP}} grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a {{ill|National Government Parks|en|National Government Parks|WD=Q6972919|lt=National Government Park}}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}} |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher={{ill|Yoshinogari site|en|Yoshinogari site|WD=Q1049645|lt=Yoshinogari Historical Park}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|en|Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|WD=Q711685|lt=Nagoya Castle}} ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|WD=Q738275|lt=Karatsu}}, {{ill|Genkai, Saga|en|Genkai, Saga|WD=Q1206926|lt=Genkai}} || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 {{ill|Hectare|en|Hectare|WD=Q35852|lt=ha}}; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the {{ill|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|en|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|WD=Q4801489|lt=Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum}} || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Kii Castle|en|Kii Castle|WD=Q11426463|lt=Kii Castle}} ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || {{ill|Kiyama, Saga|en|Kiyama, Saga|WD=Q1206602|lt=Kiyama}} || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|WD=Q28456|lt=Silla}}-{{ill|Tang dynasty|en|Tang dynasty|WD=Q9683|lt=Tang}} forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Kiyama, Saga|en|Kiyama, Saga|WD=Q1206602|lt=Kiyama Town}} |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925155809/http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |archive-date=25 September 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.town.kiyama.saga.jp/site/k-kimama/kiijo.html |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Chikushino, Fukuoka|en|Chikushino, Fukuoka|WD=Q844140|lt=Chikushino City}} |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite book |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |author=Aston, W.G. |author-link=William George Aston |year=1972 |orig-year=1896 |publisher=[[Tuttle Publishing|Tuttle]] |isbn=0-8048-0984-4 |volume=2 |pages=283f}} the designation includes an area of {{ill|Chikushino, Fukuoka|en|Chikushino, Fukuoka|WD=Q844140|lt=Chikushino}} in {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture}} || [[File:基山 山頂.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44347145|N|130.51252934|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kii Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3085] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Otsuboyama Kōgoishi|en|Otsuboyama Kōgoishi|WD=Q126723444|lt=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}}
{{nihongo2|おつぼ山神籠石}}
''Otsuboyama kōgoishi'' || {{ill|Takeo, Saga|en|Takeo, Saga|WD=Q877220|lt=Takeo}} || earthworks stretching 1,866 m, with stone pillar bases and [[:en:sluice gates|sluice gates]]; there is a theory that construction was related to defeat at the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663{{cite web |url=http://www.city.takeo.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/pages/bunkazai/bunkazai-106.htm |script-title=ja:おつぼ山神籠石 |trans-title=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Takeo, Saga|en|Takeo, Saga|WD=Q877220|lt=Takeo City}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Otsuboyama Kogoishi first water gate from side.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.17811724|N|130.05648151|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2722] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Yasunagata Site|en|Yasunagata Site|WD=Q105109472|lt=Yasunagata Site}}
{{nihongo2|安永田遺跡}}
''Yasunagata iseki'' || {{ill|Tosu, Saga|en|Tosu, Saga|WD=Q860674|lt=Tosu}} || {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|WD=Q207858|lt=Yayoi-period}} {{nihongo|"high-tech factory"|ハイテク工場}}; bronze-casting site, discovered in 1974 and extending over an area of 4,400 m2, with five moulds for {{ill|Dōtaku|en|Dōtaku|WD=Q2312868|lt=Dōtaku}} (bells) and five for {{ill|Hoko yari|en|Hoko yari|WD=Q5878224|lt=hoko}} (spears); traces of bronze found on the valley floor suggest this may have been the site of the smelting works{{cite web |url=http://www.city.tosu.lg.jp/1393.htm |script-title=ja:安永田遺跡 |trans-title=Yasunagata Site |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Tosu, Saga|en|Tosu, Saga|WD=Q860674|lt=Tosu City}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yasunagata Remains Park 20170423-1.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.39864472|N|130.51458072|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yasunagata Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2728] |- | align="center"|[[Yokotashimo Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|横田下古墳}}
''Yokotashimo kofun'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|WD=Q738275|lt=Karatsu}} || [[kofun]] or Kofun with red walls and three stone sarcophagi in which were found, in 1923, bronze mirrors and cylinders, [[magatama]] (comma-shaped beads), iron arrowheads, armour, and {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}}{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |script-title=ja:横田下古墳 |trans-title=Yokotashimo Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121218234239/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |archive-date=18 December 2012 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki02.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 02 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 2 |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.43447582|N|130.03355397|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yokotashimo Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2718] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Kakiemon|en|Kakiemon|WD=Q1721885|lt=Kakiemon Kiln Site}}
{{nihongo2|柿右衛門窯跡}}
''Kakiemon kama ato'' || {{ill|Arita, Saga|en|Arita, Saga|WD=Q668427|lt=Arita}} || double {{ill|Anagama kiln|en|Anagama kiln|WD=Q483929|lt=climbing kiln}}: A, with 12 firing chambers, a length of 42 metres, and an average incline of 11.5°; and B, with 21 chambers, a length of 83 metres, and an average gradient of 13°; {{ill|saggar|en|saggar|WD=Q3099752|lt=saggar}}s and kiln tools have also been recovered{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=173325 |script-title=ja:柿右衛門窯跡 |trans-title=Kakiemon Kiln Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Kakiemon 01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.18093825|N|129.86871429|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kakiemon Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2731] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Nabatake Site|en|Nabatake Site|WD=Q11619976|lt=Nabatake Site}}
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:菜畑遺跡|菜畑遺跡]]}}
''Nabatake iseki'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|WD=Q738275|lt=Karatsu}} || acclaimed as Japan's first {{ill|Paddy field|en|Paddy field|WD=Q842623|lt=paddy}}; important for the understanding of the adoption of wet-rice technology, introduced from the continent; focus of the {{ill|Matsurokan|en|Matsurokan|WD=Q4902941|lt=Matsurokan}} exhibition hall ||[[File:Nabatake Site rice field.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44858876|N|129.95790471|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2729] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Mietsu Naval Dock|en|Mietsu Naval Dock|WD=Q11357710|lt=Mietsu Naval Dock}} Site
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:三重津海軍所|三重津海軍所]]跡}}
''Mietsu kaigunsho ato'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || inscribed on the {{ill|List of World Heritage Sites in Japan|en|List of World Heritage Sites in Japan|WD=Q1156968|lt=UNESCO World Heritage List}} as one of the [[:en:Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining|Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/ |title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 August 2019}} || [[File:Mietsu Naval Dock view south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.207732|N|130.340137|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003786] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Anegawa Castle|en|Anegawa Castle|WD=Q11447271|lt=Anegawa Castle}} ruins

[[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] {{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the {{ill|Prefectures of Japan|en|Prefectures of Japan|WD=Q50337|lt=Prefecture}} of '''{{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga}}'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q858308|lt=designated}} as being of national {{ill|Values (heritage)|en|Values (heritage)|WD=Q7912786|lt=significance}} (including three *{{ill|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|en|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|WD=Q20982902|lt=Special Historic Sites}}); {{ill|Kii Castle|en|Kii Castle|WD=Q11426463|lt=Kii Castle}} spans the prefectural borders with {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka}}.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}} |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Yoshinogari site|en|Yoshinogari site|WD=Q1049645|lt=Yoshinogari Site}}
{{nihongo2|吉野ヶ里遺跡}}
''Yoshinogari iseki'' || {{ill|Kanzaki, Saga|en|Kanzaki, Saga|WD=Q990392|lt=Kanzaki}}, {{ill|Yoshinogari, Saga|en|Yoshinogari, Saga|WD=Q1206915|lt=Yoshinogari}} || fortified {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|WD=Q207858|lt=Yayoi-period}} settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=ICP}} grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a {{ill|National Government Parks|en|National Government Parks|WD=Q6972919|lt=National Government Park}}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}} |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher={{ill|Yoshinogari site|en|Yoshinogari site|WD=Q1049645|lt=Yoshinogari Historical Park}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|en|Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|WD=Q711685|lt=Nagoya Castle}} ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|WD=Q738275|lt=Karatsu}}, {{ill|Genkai, Saga|en|Genkai, Saga|WD=Q1206926|lt=Genkai}} || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 {{ill|Hectare|en|Hectare|WD=Q35852|lt=ha}}; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the {{ill|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|en|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|WD=Q4801489|lt=Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum}} || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Kii Castle|en|Kii Castle|WD=Q11426463|lt=Kii Castle}} ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || {{ill|Kiyama, Saga|en|Kiyama, Saga|WD=Q1206602|lt=Kiyama}} || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|WD=Q28456|lt=Silla}}-{{ill|Tang dynasty|en|Tang dynasty|WD=Q9683|lt=Tang}} forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Kiyama, Saga|en|Kiyama, Saga|WD=Q1206602|lt=Kiyama Town}} |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925155809/http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |archive-date=25 September 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.town.kiyama.saga.jp/site/k-kimama/kiijo.html |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Chikushino, Fukuoka|en|Chikushino, Fukuoka|WD=Q844140|lt=Chikushino City}} |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite book |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |author=Aston, W.G. |author-link=William George Aston |year=1972 |orig-year=1896 |publisher=[[Tuttle Publishing|Tuttle]] |isbn=0-8048-0984-4 |volume=2 |pages=283f}} the designation includes an area of {{ill|Chikushino, Fukuoka|en|Chikushino, Fukuoka|WD=Q844140|lt=Chikushino}} in {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture}} || [[File:基山 山頂.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44347145|N|130.51252934|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kii Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3085] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Otsuboyama Kōgoishi|en|Otsuboyama Kōgoishi|WD=Q126723444|lt=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}}
{{nihongo2|おつぼ山神籠石}}
''Otsuboyama kōgoishi'' || {{ill|Takeo, Saga|en|Takeo, Saga|WD=Q877220|lt=Takeo}} || earthworks stretching 1,866 m, with stone pillar bases and [[:en:sluice gates|sluice gates]]; there is a theory that construction was related to defeat at the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663{{cite web |url=http://www.city.takeo.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/pages/bunkazai/bunkazai-106.htm |script-title=ja:おつぼ山神籠石 |trans-title=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Takeo, Saga|en|Takeo, Saga|WD=Q877220|lt=Takeo City}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Otsuboyama Kogoishi first water gate from side.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.17811724|N|130.05648151|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2722] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Yasunagata Site|en|Yasunagata Site|WD=Q105109472|lt=Yasunagata Site}}
{{nihongo2|安永田遺跡}}
''Yasunagata iseki'' || {{ill|Tosu, Saga|en|Tosu, Saga|WD=Q860674|lt=Tosu}} || {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|WD=Q207858|lt=Yayoi-period}} {{nihongo|"high-tech factory"|ハイテク工場}}; bronze-casting site, discovered in 1974 and extending over an area of 4,400 m2, with five moulds for {{ill|Dōtaku|en|Dōtaku|WD=Q2312868|lt=Dōtaku}} (bells) and five for {{ill|Hoko yari|en|Hoko yari|WD=Q5878224|lt=hoko}} (spears); traces of bronze found on the valley floor suggest this may have been the site of the smelting works{{cite web |url=http://www.city.tosu.lg.jp/1393.htm |script-title=ja:安永田遺跡 |trans-title=Yasunagata Site |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Tosu, Saga|en|Tosu, Saga|WD=Q860674|lt=Tosu City}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yasunagata Remains Park 20170423-1.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.39864472|N|130.51458072|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yasunagata Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2728] |- | align="center"|[[Yokotashimo Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|横田下古墳}}
''Yokotashimo kofun'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|WD=Q738275|lt=Karatsu}} || [[kofun]] or Kofun with red walls and three stone sarcophagi in which were found, in 1923, bronze mirrors and cylinders, [[magatama]] (comma-shaped beads), iron arrowheads, armour, and {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery}}{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |script-title=ja:横田下古墳 |trans-title=Yokotashimo Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121218234239/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |archive-date=18 December 2012 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki02.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 02 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 2 |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.43447582|N|130.03355397|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yokotashimo Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2718] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Kakiemon|en|Kakiemon|WD=Q1721885|lt=Kakiemon Kiln Site}}
{{nihongo2|柿右衛門窯跡}}
''Kakiemon kama ato'' || {{ill|Arita, Saga|en|Arita, Saga|WD=Q668427|lt=Arita}} || double {{ill|Anagama kiln|en|Anagama kiln|WD=Q483929|lt=climbing kiln}}: A, with 12 firing chambers, a length of 42 metres, and an average incline of 11.5°; and B, with 21 chambers, a length of 83 metres, and an average gradient of 13°; {{ill|saggar|en|saggar|WD=Q3099752|lt=saggar}}s and kiln tools have also been recovered{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=173325 |script-title=ja:柿右衛門窯跡 |trans-title=Kakiemon Kiln Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Kakiemon 01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.18093825|N|129.86871429|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kakiemon Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2731] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Nabatake Site|en|Nabatake Site|WD=Q11619976|lt=Nabatake Site}}
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:菜畑遺跡|菜畑遺跡]]}}
''Nabatake iseki'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|WD=Q738275|lt=Karatsu}} || acclaimed as Japan's first {{ill|Paddy field|en|Paddy field|WD=Q842623|lt=paddy}}; important for the understanding of the adoption of wet-rice technology, introduced from the continent; focus of the {{ill|Matsurokan|en|Matsurokan|WD=Q4902941|lt=Matsurokan}} exhibition hall ||[[File:Nabatake Site rice field.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44858876|N|129.95790471|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2729] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Mietsu Naval Dock|en|Mietsu Naval Dock|WD=Q11357710|lt=Mietsu Naval Dock}} Site
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:三重津海軍所|三重津海軍所]]跡}}
''Mietsu kaigunsho ato'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || inscribed on the {{ill|List of World Heritage Sites in Japan|en|List of World Heritage Sites in Japan|WD=Q1156968|lt=UNESCO World Heritage List}} as one of the [[:en:Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining|Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/ |title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 August 2019}} || [[File:Mietsu Naval Dock view south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.207732|N|130.340137|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003786] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Anegawa Castle|en|Anegawa Castle|WD=Q11447271|lt=Anegawa Castle}} ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:姉川城|姉川城]]跡}}
''Anegawa-jō ato'' || {{ill|Kanzaki, Saga|en|Kanzaki, Saga|WD=Q990392|lt=Kanzaki}} || strategic site under {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|en|Ryūzōji Takanobu|WD=Q1076150|lt=Ryūzōji Takanobu}} but declined in importance after the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi#Pinnacle of power|unification of Kyūshū by Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]; the site extends 600 metres E-W and 800 N-S, with related mansions, temples and shrines, and a complex network of moats{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki03.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 3 |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}} |access-date=14 June 2012}}||[[File:Anegawa Castle Ruins south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.29314988|N|130.34839565|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Anegawa Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003663] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Katsunoo Castle|en|Katsunoo Castle|WD=Q11400221|lt=Katsunoo Castle Tsukushi Clan Sites}}
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:勝尾城|勝尾城]][[:ja:筑紫氏|筑紫氏]]遺跡}}
''Katsuno-jō Tsukushi-shi iseki'' || {{ill|Tosu, Saga|en|Tosu, Saga|WD=Q860674|lt=Tosu}} || fortified at the end of the fifteenth century; attacked by the {{ill|Shimazu clan|en|Shimazu clan|WD=Q1061406|lt=Shimazu clan}} in 1586 and later abandoned; excavations from 1995 have revealed an extensive site with moats, earthworks, mansions for retainers, temples and shrines{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=140467 |title=勝尾城筑紫氏遺跡 |trans-title=Katsuno Castle Tsukushi Clan Sites |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=16 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.40213518|N|130.46524915|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Katsuno Castle Chikushi Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003477] |- | align="center"|[[Nishikuma Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|西隈古墳}}
''Nishikuma kofun'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || C5 [[decorated kofun]] housing a large sarcophagus, with red pigmentation and incised decoration of triangles and circles{{cite web |url=http://kyuhaku.jmc.or.jp/d_frame.php/41/6/ |script-title=ja:西隈古墳 |trans-title=Nishikuma Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Kyushu National Museum]] |access-date=9 December 2013}} || [[File:Nishikuma-kofun stone wall.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32738344|N|130.29346106|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nishikuma Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2725] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Taku Seibyō|en|Taku Seibyō|WD=Q2278548|lt=Taku Seibyō}}
{{nihongo2|多久聖廟}}
''Taku Seibyō'' || {{ill|Taku, Saga|en|Taku, Saga|WD=Q877177|lt=Taku}} || a [[:en:Edo Neo-Confucianism|Neo-Confucian]] school was established by {{nihongo|Taku Shigefumi|[[:ja:多久茂文|多久茂文]]}} in 1699; the {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=ICP}} temple dates to 1708; [[Conservation Techniques for Cultural Properties|major repairs]] at the end of the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Shōwa era}} were completed in 1990{{cite web |url=http://www.city.taku.lg.jp/site/view/contview.jsp?cateid=12&id=373&page=1 |script-title=ja:多久聖廟 |trans-title=Taku Seibyō |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Taku, Saga|en|Taku, Saga|WD=Q877177|lt=Taku City}} |access-date=14 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3509 |script-title=ja:多久聖廟 |trans-title=Taku Seibyō |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 June 2012}} ||| [[File:Taku Seibyo 02.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.25974392|N|130.09758673|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Taku Seibyō}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|4]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2704] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Obukumayama Kōgoishi|en|Obukumayama Kōgoishi|WD=Q105814630|lt=Obukumayama Kōgoishi}}
{{nihongo2|帯隈山神籠石}}
''Obukumayama kōgoishi'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || C7 fortifications discovered in 1941, that extend for 2.4 km and include a gate || [[File:Obukumayama Kōgoishi arranged stones.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.33361745|N|130.33454194|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Obukumayama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2717] |- | align="center"|[[Ōkuma Shigenobu#Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence|Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence]]
{{nihongo2|大隈重信旧宅}}
''Ōkuma Shigenobu kyū-taku'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || birthplace in 1838 of the {{ill|Meiji era|en|Meiji era|WD=Q3125096|lt=Meiji}} statesman and future [[:en:prime minister of Japan|prime minister]]; dismantled for repairs in 1968 and open to the public alongside the {{nihongo|Ōkuma Memorial Museum|大隈記念館}} || [[File:Okuma Shigenobu Kyutaku.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.24812272|N|130.30848099|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Ōkuma Shigenobu Former Residence}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|8]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2725] |- | align="center"|[[Nabeshima ware#Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site|Ōkawachi Nabeshima Kiln Site]]
{{nihongo2|大川内鍋島窯跡}}

[[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] {{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the {{ill|Prefectures of Japan|en|Prefectures of Japan|WD=Q50337|lt=Prefecture}} of '''{{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga}}'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q858308|lt=designated}} as being of national {{ill|Values (heritage)|en|Values (heritage)|WD=Q7912786|lt=significance}} (including three *{{ill|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|en|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|WD=Q20982902|lt=Special Historic Sites}}); {{ill|Kii Castle|en|Kii Castle|WD=Q11426463|lt=Kii Castle}} spans the prefectural borders with {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka}}.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}} |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Yoshinogari site|en|Yoshinogari site|WD=Q1049645|lt=Yoshinogari Site}}
{{nihongo2|吉野ヶ里遺跡}}
''Yoshinogari iseki'' || {{ill|Kanzaki, Saga|en|Kanzaki, Saga|WD=Q990392|lt=Kanzaki}}, {{ill|Yoshinogari, Saga|en|Yoshinogari, Saga|WD=Q1206915|lt=Yoshinogari}} || fortified {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|WD=Q207858|lt=Yayoi-period}} settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=ICP}} grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a {{ill|National Government Parks|en|National Government Parks|WD=Q6972919|lt=National Government Park}}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture}} |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher={{ill|Yoshinogari site|en|Yoshinogari site|WD=Q1049645|lt=Yoshinogari Historical Park}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|en|Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|WD=Q711685|lt=Nagoya Castle}} ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|WD=Q738275|lt=Karatsu}}, {{ill|Genkai, Saga|en|Genkai, Saga|WD=Q1206926|lt=Genkai}} || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 {{ill|Hectare|en|Hectare|WD=Q35852|lt=ha}}; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the {{ill|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|en|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|WD=Q4801489|lt=Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum}} || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Kii Castle|en|Kii Castle|WD=Q11426463|lt=Kii Castle}} ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || {{ill|Kiyama, Saga|en|Kiyama, Saga|WD=Q1206602|lt=Kiyama}} || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|WD=Q28456|lt=Silla}}-{{ill|Tang dynasty|en|Tang dynasty|WD=Q9683|lt=Tang}} forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Kiyama, Saga|en|Kiyama, Saga|WD=Q1206602|lt=Kiyama Town}} |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925155809/http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |archive-date=25 September 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.town.kiyama.saga.jp/site/k-kimama/kiijo.html |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Chikushino, Fukuoka|en|Chikushino, Fukuoka|WD=Q844140|lt=Chikushino City}} |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite book |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |author=Aston, W.G. |author-link=William George Aston |year=1972 |orig-year=1896 |publisher=[[Tuttle Publishing|Tuttle]] |isbn=0-8048-0984-4 |volume=2 |pages=283f}} the designation includes an area of {{ill|Chikushino, Fukuoka|en|Chikushino, Fukuoka|WD=Q844140|lt=Chikushino}} in {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture}} || [[File:基山 山頂.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44347145|N|130.51252934|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kii Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3085] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Otsuboyama Kōgoishi|en|Otsuboyama Kōgoishi|WD=Q126723444|lt=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}}

''Kurisōzui kofun'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|WD=Q738275|lt=Karatsu}} || || [[File:Kuri Souzui Kofun01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.396816|N|129.986507|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kurisōzui Kofun}} || || [http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/kiji0031643/index.html] |- |} ==Municipal Historic Sites== As of 1 May 2018, a further eighty-one Sites have been designated as being of municipal importance.{{cite web|url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/chiho_shitei/shichoson.html |title=都道府県別指定等文化財件数（市町村分）|trans-title=Number of Municipal Cultural Properties by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 May 2018 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {{Historic Sites of Japan}} ==See also== {{portal|Japan}} {{Commons Category|National historic sites in Saga prefecture}} {{Commons Category|Prefectural Historic Sites in Saga Prefecture}} * {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q858308|lt=Cultural Property (Japan)}} * {{ill|Hizen Province|en|Hizen Province|WD=Q906926|lt=Hizen Province}} * {{ill|Saga Domain|en|Saga Domain|WD=Q2975995|lt=Saga Domain}} * {{ill|Saga Prefectural Museum|en|Saga Prefectural Museum|WD=Q6371422|lt=Saga Prefectural Museum}} * [[:en:List of Cultural Properties of Japan -
