[[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] {{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the {{ill|Prefectures of Japan|en|Prefectures of Japan|WD=Q50337|lt=Prefecture|1=Prefectures of Japan}} of '''{{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga|1=Saga Prefecture}}'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q858308|lt=designated|1=Cultural Property (Japan)}} as being of national {{ill|Values (heritage)|en|Values (heritage)|WD=Q7912786|lt=significance|1=Values (heritage)}} (including three *{{ill|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|en|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|WD=Q20982902|lt=Special Historic Sites|1=List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments}}); {{ill|Kii Castle|en|Kii Castle|WD=Q11426463|lt=Kii Castle|1=Kii Castle}} spans the prefectural borders with {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}}.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture|1=Saga Prefecture}} |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Yoshinogari site|en|Yoshinogari site|WD=Q1049645|lt=Yoshinogari Site|1=Yoshinogari site}}
{{nihongo2|吉野ヶ里遺跡}}
''Yoshinogari iseki'' || {{ill|Kanzaki, Saga|en|Kanzaki, Saga|WD=Q990392|lt=Kanzaki|1=Kanzaki, Saga}}, {{ill|Yoshinogari, Saga|en|Yoshinogari, Saga|WD=Q1206915|lt=Yoshinogari|1=Yoshinogari, Saga}} || fortified {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|WD=Q207858|lt=Yayoi-period|1=Yayoi period}} settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=ICP|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a {{ill|National Government Parks|en|National Government Parks|WD=Q6972919|lt=National Government Park|1=National Government Parks}}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture|1=Saga Prefecture}} |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher={{ill|Yoshinogari site|en|Yoshinogari site|WD=Q1049645|lt=Yoshinogari Historical Park|1=Yoshinogari site}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|en|Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|WD=Q711685|lt=Nagoya Castle|1=Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)}} ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|WD=Q738275|lt=Karatsu|1=Karatsu, Saga}}, {{ill|Genkai, Saga|en|Genkai, Saga|WD=Q1206926|lt=Genkai|1=Genkai, Saga}} || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 {{ill|Hectare|en|Hectare|WD=Q35852|lt=ha|1=Hectare}}; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the {{ill|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|en|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|WD=Q4801489|lt=Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|1=Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum}} || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Kii Castle|en|Kii Castle|WD=Q11426463|lt=Kii Castle|1=Kii Castle}} ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || {{ill|Kiyama, Saga|en|Kiyama, Saga|WD=Q1206602|lt=Kiyama|1=Kiyama, Saga}} || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|WD=Q28456|lt=Silla|1=Silla}}-{{ill|Tang dynasty|en|Tang dynasty|WD=Q9683|lt=Tang|1=Tang dynasty}} forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Kiyama, Saga|en|Kiyama, Saga|WD=Q1206602|lt=Kiyama Town|1=Kiyama, Saga}} |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100925155809/http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |archive-date=25 September 2010 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.town.kiyama.saga.jp/site/k-kimama/kiijo.html |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Chikushino, Fukuoka|en|Chikushino, Fukuoka|WD=Q844140|lt=Chikushino City|1=Chikushino, Fukuoka}} |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite book |title=Nihongi: Chronicles of Japan from the Earliest Times to A.D. 697 |author=Aston, W.G. |author-link=William George Aston |year=1972 |orig-year=1896 |publisher=[[Tuttle Publishing|Tuttle]] |isbn=0-8048-0984-4 |volume=2 |pages=283f}} the designation includes an area of {{ill|Chikushino, Fukuoka|en|Chikushino, Fukuoka|WD=Q844140|lt=Chikushino|1=Chikushino, Fukuoka}} in {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|WD=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka Prefecture|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}} || [[File:基山 山頂.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44347145|N|130.51252934|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kii Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/3085] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Otsuboyama Kōgoishi|en|Otsuboyama Kōgoishi|WD=Q126723444|lt=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi|1=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}}
{{nihongo2|おつぼ山神籠石}}
''Otsuboyama kōgoishi'' || {{ill|Takeo, Saga|en|Takeo, Saga|WD=Q877220|lt=Takeo|1=Takeo, Saga}} || earthworks stretching 1,866 m, with stone pillar bases and [[:en:sluice gates|sluice gates]]; there is a theory that construction was related to defeat at the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663{{cite web |url=http://www.city.takeo.lg.jp/kyouiku/bunkazai/pages/bunkazai/bunkazai-106.htm |script-title=ja:おつぼ山神籠石 |trans-title=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Takeo, Saga|en|Takeo, Saga|WD=Q877220|lt=Takeo City|1=Takeo, Saga}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Otsuboyama Kogoishi first water gate from side.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.17811724|N|130.05648151|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Otsuboyama Kōgoishi}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2722] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Yasunagata Site|en|Yasunagata Site|WD=Q105109472|lt=Yasunagata Site|1=Yasunagata Site}}
{{nihongo2|安永田遺跡}}
''Yasunagata iseki'' || {{ill|Tosu, Saga|en|Tosu, Saga|WD=Q860674|lt=Tosu|1=Tosu, Saga}} || {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|WD=Q207858|lt=Yayoi-period|1=Yayoi period}} {{nihongo|"high-tech factory"|ハイテク工場}}; bronze-casting site, discovered in 1974 and extending over an area of 4,400 m2, with five moulds for {{ill|Dōtaku|en|Dōtaku|WD=Q2312868|lt=Dōtaku|1=Dōtaku}} (bells) and five for {{ill|Hoko yari|en|Hoko yari|WD=Q5878224|lt=hoko|1=Hoko yari}} (spears); traces of bronze found on the valley floor suggest this may have been the site of the smelting works{{cite web |url=http://www.city.tosu.lg.jp/1393.htm |script-title=ja:安永田遺跡 |trans-title=Yasunagata Site |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Tosu, Saga|en|Tosu, Saga|WD=Q860674|lt=Tosu City|1=Tosu, Saga}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yasunagata Remains Park 20170423-1.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.39864472|N|130.51458072|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yasunagata Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2728] |- | align="center"|[[Yokotashimo Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|横田下古墳}}
''Yokotashimo kofun'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|WD=Q738275|lt=Karatsu|1=Karatsu, Saga}} || [[kofun]] or Kofun with red walls and three stone sarcophagi in which were found, in 1923, bronze mirrors and cylinders, [[magatama]] (comma-shaped beads), iron arrowheads, armour, and {{ill|Haji pottery|en|Haji pottery|WD=Q5639938|lt=Haji pottery|1=Haji pottery}}{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |script-title=ja:横田下古墳 |trans-title=Yokotashimo Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121218234239/http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/db/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=192012 |archive-date=18 December 2012 }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki02.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 02 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 2 |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture|1=Saga Prefecture}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.43447582|N|130.03355397|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yokotashimo Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2718] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Kakiemon|en|Kakiemon|WD=Q1721885|lt=Kakiemon Kiln Site|1=Kakiemon}}
{{nihongo2|柿右衛門窯跡}}
''Kakiemon kama ato'' || {{ill|Arita, Saga|en|Arita, Saga|WD=Q668427|lt=Arita|1=Arita, Saga}} || double {{ill|Anagama kiln|en|Anagama kiln|WD=Q483929|lt=climbing kiln|1=Anagama kiln}}: A, with 12 firing chambers, a length of 42 metres, and an average incline of 11.5°; and B, with 21 chambers, a length of 83 metres, and an average gradient of 13°; {{ill|saggar|en|saggar|WD=Q3099752|lt=saggar|1=Saggar}}s and kiln tools have also been recovered{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=173325 |script-title=ja:柿右衛門窯跡 |trans-title=Kakiemon Kiln Site |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Kakiemon 01.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.18093825|N|129.86871429|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Kakiemon Kiln Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|6]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2731] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Nabatake Site|en|Nabatake Site|WD=Q11619976|lt=Nabatake Site|1=Nabatake Site}}
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:菜畑遺跡|菜畑遺跡]]}}
''Nabatake iseki'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|WD=Q738275|lt=Karatsu|1=Karatsu, Saga}} || acclaimed as Japan's first {{ill|Paddy field|en|Paddy field|WD=Q842623|lt=paddy|1=Paddy field}}; important for the understanding of the adoption of wet-rice technology, introduced from the continent; focus of the {{ill|Matsurokan|en|Matsurokan|WD=Q4902941|lt=Matsurokan|1=Matsurokan}} exhibition hall ||[[File:Nabatake Site rice field.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.44858876|N|129.95790471|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2729] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Mietsu Naval Dock|en|Mietsu Naval Dock|WD=Q11357710|lt=Mietsu Naval Dock|1=Mietsu Naval Dock}} Site
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:三重津海軍所|三重津海軍所]]跡}}
''Mietsu kaigunsho ato'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || inscribed on the {{ill|List of World Heritage Sites in Japan|en|List of World Heritage Sites in Japan|WD=Q1156968|lt=UNESCO World Heritage List|1=List of World Heritage Sites in Japan}} as one of the [[:en:Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining|Sites of Japan’s Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining]]{{cite web |url=https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/1484/ |title=Sites of Japan's Meiji Industrial Revolution: Iron and Steel, Shipbuilding and Coal Mining |publisher=[[UNESCO]] |access-date=5 August 2019}} || [[File:Mietsu Naval Dock view south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.207732|N|130.340137|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nabatake Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003786] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Anegawa Castle|en|Anegawa Castle|WD=Q11447271|lt=Anegawa Castle|1=Anegawa Castle}} ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:姉川城|姉川城]]跡}}
''Anegawa-jō ato'' || {{ill|Kanzaki, Saga|en|Kanzaki, Saga|WD=Q990392|lt=Kanzaki|1=Kanzaki, Saga}} || strategic site under {{ill|Ryūzōji Takanobu|en|Ryūzōji Takanobu|WD=Q1076150|lt=Ryūzōji Takanobu|1=Ryūzōji Takanobu}} but declined in importance after the [[Toyotomi Hideyoshi#Pinnacle of power|unification of Kyūshū by Toyotomi Hideyoshi]]; the site extends 600 metres E-W and 800 N-S, with related mansions, temples and shrines, and a complex network of moats{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki03.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 3 |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|WD=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture|1=Saga Prefecture}} |access-date=14 June 2012}}||[[File:Anegawa Castle Ruins south.JPG|150px]] || {{coord|33.29314988|N|130.34839565|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Anegawa Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003663] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Katsunoo Castle|en|Katsunoo Castle|WD=Q11400221|lt=Katsunoo Castle Tsukushi Clan Sites|1=Katsunoo Castle}}
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:勝尾城|勝尾城]][[:ja:筑紫氏|筑紫氏]]遺跡}}
''Katsuno-jō Tsukushi-shi iseki'' || {{ill|Tosu, Saga|en|Tosu, Saga|WD=Q860674|lt=Tosu|1=Tosu, Saga}} || fortified at the end of the fifteenth century; attacked by the {{ill|Shimazu clan|en|Shimazu clan|WD=Q1061406|lt=Shimazu clan|1=Shimazu clan}} in 1586 and later abandoned; excavations from 1995 have revealed an extensive site with moats, earthworks, mansions for retainers, temples and shrines{{cite web |url=http://bunka.nii.ac.jp/SearchDetail.do?heritageId=140467 |title=勝尾城筑紫氏遺跡 |trans-title=Katsuno Castle Tsukushi Clan Sites |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=16 June 2012}} || || {{coord|33.40213518|N|130.46524915|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Katsuno Castle Chikushi Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/00003477] |- | align="center"|[[Nishikuma Kofun]]
{{nihongo2|西隈古墳}}
''Nishikuma kofun'' || [[:en:Saga, Saga|Saga]] || C5 [[decorated kofun]] housing a large sarcophagus, with red pigmentation and incised decoration of triangles and circles{{cite web |url=http://kyuhaku.jmc.or.jp/d_frame.php/41/6/ |script-title=ja:西隈古墳 |trans-title=Nishikuma Kofun |language=ja |publisher=[[Kyushu National Museum]] |access-date=9 December 2013}} || [[File:Nishikuma-kofun stone wall.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32738344|N|130.29346106|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nishikuma Kofun}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2725] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Taku Seibyō|en|Taku Seibyō|WD=Q2278548|lt=Taku Seibyō|1=Taku Seibyō}}
{{nihongo2|多久聖廟}}
''Taku Seibyō'' || {{ill|Taku, Saga|en|Taku, Saga|WD=Q877177|lt=Taku|1=Taku, Saga}} || a [[:en:Edo Neo-Confucianism|Neo-Confucian]] school was established by {{nihongo|Taku Shigefumi|[[:ja:多久茂文|多久茂文]]}} in 1699; the {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|WD=Q1188622|lt=ICP|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} temple dates to 1708; [[Conservation Techniques for Cultural Properties|major repairs]] at the end of the {{ill|Shōwa era|en|Shōwa era|WD=Q327567|lt=Shōwa era|1=Shōwa era}} were completed in 1990{{cite web |url=http://www.city.taku.lg.jp/site/view/contview.jsp?cateid=12&id=373&page=1 |script-title=ja:多久聖廟 |trans-title=Taku Seibyō |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Taku, Saga|en|Taku, Saga|WD=Q877177|lt=Taku City|1=Taku, Saga}} |access-date=14 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/102/3509 |script-title=ja:多久聖廟 |trans-title=Taku Seibyō |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=14 June 2012}} ||| [[File:Taku Seibyo 02.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.25974392|N|130.09758673|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Taku Seibyō}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|4]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2704] |- | align="center"|{{ill|Obukumayama Kōgoishi|en|Obukumayama Kōgoishi|WD=Q105814630|lt=Obukumayama Kōgoishi|1=Obukumayama Kōgoishi}}
{{nihongo2|帯隈山神籠石}}

[[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] [[en:List of Historic Sites of Japan (Saga)]] {{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the {{ill|Prefectures of Japan|en|Prefectures of Japan|qid=Q50337|lt=Prefecture|1=Prefectures of Japan}} of '''{{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|qid=Q160420|lt=Saga|1=Saga Prefecture}}'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q858308|lt=designated|1=Cultural Property (Japan)}} as being of national {{ill|Values (heritage)|en|Values (heritage)|qid=Q7912786|lt=significance|1=Values (heritage)}} (including three *{{ill|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|en|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|qid=Q20982902|lt=Special Historic Sites|1=List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments}}); {{ill|Kii Castle|en|Kii Castle|qid=Q11426463|lt=Kii Castle|1=Kii Castle}} spans the prefectural borders with {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|qid=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}}.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|qid=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture|1=Saga Prefecture}} |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Yoshinogari site|en|Yoshinogari site|qid=Q1049645|lt=Yoshinogari Site|1=Yoshinogari site}}

{{short description|None}} {{GeoGroup}} This list is of the '''[[Monuments of Japan|Historic Sites of Japan]]''' located within the {{ill|Prefectures of Japan|en|Prefectures of Japan|qid=Q50337|lt=Prefecture|1=Prefectures of Japan}} of '''{{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|qid=Q160420|lt=Saga|1=Saga Prefecture}}'''.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/tokei_hakusho_shuppan/shuppanbutsu/bunkazai_pamphlet/pamphlet_en.html |title=Cultural Properties for Future Generations |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=3 August 2019}} ==National Historic Sites== As of 1 August 2019, twenty-five Sites have been {{ill|Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q858308|lt=designated|1=Cultural Property (Japan)}} as being of national {{ill|Values (heritage)|en|Values (heritage)|qid=Q7912786|lt=significance|1=Values (heritage)}} (including three *{{ill|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|en|List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments|qid=Q20982902|lt=Special Historic Sites|1=List of Special Places of Scenic Beauty, Special Historic Sites and Special Natural Monuments}}); {{ill|Kii Castle|en|Kii Castle|qid=Q11426463|lt=Kii Castle|1=Kii Castle}} spans the prefectural borders with {{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|en|Fukuoka Prefecture|qid=Q123258|lt=Fukuoka|1=Fukuoka Prefecture}}.{{cite web |url=http://www.bunka.go.jp/seisaku/bunkazai/shokai/shitei.html |script-title=ja:史跡名勝天然記念物 |trans-title=Number of Monuments of Japan by Prefecture |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |date=1 July 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}}{{cite web |url=http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |title=Database of National Cultural Properties: 史跡名勝天然記念物 (史跡, 特別史跡 佐賀県 2県以上) |language=ja |publisher=[[Agency for Cultural Affairs]] |access-date=5 August 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170502003537/http://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/bsys/index_pc.html |archive-date=2 May 2017 |url-status=dead }}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/kensaku_kensuu.html |script-title=ja:佐賀県内所在指定文化財等件数一覧 |trans-title=Number of Cultural Properties in Saga Prefecture |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|qid=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture|1=Saga Prefecture}} |date=1 August 2019 |access-date=5 August 2019}} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="width:100%;" |- !width="30%" align="left" | Site !width="10%" align="left" | Municipality !width="30%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Comments !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| image !width="10%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Coordinates !width="5%" align="left" | Type !width="5%" align="left" class="unsortable"| Ref. |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Yoshinogari site|en|Yoshinogari site|qid=Q1049645|lt=Yoshinogari Site|1=Yoshinogari site}}
{{nihongo2|吉野ヶ里遺跡}}
''Yoshinogari iseki'' || {{ill|Kanzaki, Saga|en|Kanzaki, Saga|qid=Q990392|lt=Kanzaki|1=Kanzaki, Saga}}, {{ill|Yoshinogari, Saga|en|Yoshinogari, Saga|qid=Q1206915|lt=Yoshinogari|1=Yoshinogari, Saga}} || fortified {{ill|Yayoi period|en|Yayoi period|qid=Q207858|lt=Yayoi-period|1=Yayoi period}} settlement, the subject of extensive excavation from 1986; 2500 burials with {{ill|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|en|Important Cultural Property (Japan)|qid=Q1188622|lt=ICP|1=Important Cultural Property (Japan)}} grave goods have been uncovered; the site has been reconstructed on the basis of hypotheses drawn from the [[postholes]]; now a {{ill|National Government Parks|en|National Government Parks|qid=Q6972919|lt=National Government Park|1=National Government Parks}}{{cite web |url=http://www.pref.saga.lg.jp/web/kankou/bunkazai/zai_top/kensaku_top/data_kuni_shiseki01.html |script-title=ja:国指定 (史跡の部) 01 |trans-title=National Historic Sites 1 |language=ja |publisher={{ill|Saga Prefecture|en|Saga Prefecture|qid=Q160420|lt=Saga Prefecture|1=Saga Prefecture}} |access-date=11 June 2012}}{{cite web |url=http://www.yoshinogari.jp/en/ |title=Yoshinogari Historical Park |publisher={{ill|Yoshinogari site|en|Yoshinogari site|qid=Q1049645|lt=Yoshinogari Historical Park|1=Yoshinogari site}} |access-date=11 June 2012}} || [[File:Yoshinogari Ancient Ruins 2008.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.32541401|N|130.38439419|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Yoshinogari Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|1]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2732] |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|en|Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)|qid=Q711685|lt=Nagoya Castle|1=Nagoya Castle (Hizen Province)}} ruins
{{nihongo2|名護屋城跡並陣跡}}
''Nagoya-jō ato narabainijin ato'' || {{ill|Karatsu, Saga|en|Karatsu, Saga|qid=Q738275|lt=Karatsu|1=Karatsu, Saga}}, {{ill|Genkai, Saga|en|Genkai, Saga|qid=Q1206926|lt=Genkai|1=Genkai, Saga}} || begun in 1591 and completed five months later; extends over 17 {{ill|Hectare|en|Hectare|qid=Q35852|lt=ha|1=Hectare}}; stone walls, earthworks, moats, gates and other buildings have been identified; served as the base for [[:en:Japanese invasions of Korea (1592–1598)|Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea]] between 1592 and 1598; focus of the {{ill|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|en|Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|qid=Q4801489|lt=Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum|1=Saga Prefectural Nagoya Castle Museum}} || [[File:NagoyaC Otemon.jpg|150px]] || {{coord|33.53035107|N|129.86811091|E|display=inline|format=dms|type:landmark_region:JP_scale:10000|name=Nagoya Castle Site}} || [[Monuments of Japan#Historic Sites and Special Historic Sites|2]] || [https://kunishitei.bunka.go.jp/heritage/detail/401/2711] |- | align="center"|*{{ill|Kii Castle|en|Kii Castle|qid=Q11426463|lt=Kii Castle|1=Kii Castle}} ruins
{{nihongo2|[[:ja:基肄城|基肄(椽)城]]跡}}
''Kii-jō ato'' || {{ill|Kiyama, Saga|en|Kiyama, Saga|qid=Q1206602|lt=Kiyama|1=Kiyama, Saga}} || its construction in 665 under [[:en:Baekje|Baekje]] guidance, as the castle of {{nihongo|Woyogi|椽}}, is chronicled in ''[[Nihon Shoki]]''; formed part of a network of defences dating to the immediate aftermath of the [[:en:Battle of Hakusukinoe|Battle of Hakusukinoe]] in 663 to protect [[:en:Dazaifu (term)|Dazaifu]] against the threat of invasion from the Korean peninsula by {{ill|Silla|en|Silla|qid=Q28456|lt=Silla|1=Silla}}-{{ill|Tang dynasty|en|Tang dynasty|qid=Q9683|lt=Tang|1=Tang dynasty}} forces;{{cite web |url=http://www.city.chikushino.fukuoka.jp/kyouikubu/bunka-shinko/kiizyou.html?print=1&temptype=1&laytype=1&itemtype=1 |script-title=ja:基肄城 |trans-title=Kii Castle |language=ja
